feature.title: Keep Older Passkey Accounts Working on Every Site

notes: Planned and de-risked on 2026-10-16; decisions 1 to 9 answered by 2026-10-17 (the plan's recommendations, with O4 settled under decision 2). Ready to promote to active; open review items O1 to O6 are in plan.todo.md.

Clean-room proof: reports/2026-10-16-clean-room-proof-fifth-review.md, which supersedes the four earlier reports of the same day (clean-room Chromium, virtual authenticator; signatures checked by read-only eth_call). Device proof (plan step 11) and the restore rehearsal before step 5 deploys (AC-13) are Afo's.
Shared auth workflows and the agent passkey directory are critical surfaces: read every touched line and keep the selector's critical override.
Never re-encode a stored passkey credential ID: Kernel hashes that exact string into the account address.

Related records: PRD-1107 built the directory; COM-39 was rewritten around this plan on 2026-10-16 (decision 8, text in handoffs/com-39-update-draft.md). Name rules belong to green-goods-name-reservation.
status.json is authoritative; set a concrete <type>/<work-description> branch only when work begins.

tdd.note: No contract change: the deployed WebAuthn validator already accepts related-origin and adopted signatures (clean-room report, scenario E).

history.note: Scaffolded feature hub in backlog
Wrote brief, spec, plan, eval, the clean-room proof report and the portable rig; contracts lane marked n/a. Timestamp: the commit that recorded it.
Decision 8 answered: Afo chose the COM-39 rewrite, which was posted the same day. Timestamp: the commit that recorded it.

Addressed the first Codex review: adoption calls run beside the hosted lookup on a no-retry, 3-second client; completion is idempotent; uniqueness is on credential bytes; a v2.0.1 upgrade test and mismatched-ID refusals are planned; wrong-site copy names the sites a hosted account may come from. Rig rerun adds admin signing and the new refusals. Timestamp: the observed rig rerun.

Addressed the second review (Codex and CodeRabbit): stored IDs match under either reading and the credential key comes from the assertion; the completion gets a 10-second deadline; positive tests planned for the hosted race and the taken-name row; the resume steps keep the decision gate; current-evidence links point at the second-review report; the rig refuses unknown modes. Timestamp: the observed rig rerun.

Addressed the third review (Codex): an idempotent completion must match the stored ID string exactly, since Kernel hashes it; the rig now refuses the held name sent with the other spelling. Timestamp: the observed rig rerun.

Addressed the fourth review (Codex): a hosted name is adopted only under the hosted server's exact ID string and key, and a hosted cross-spelling refusal joins the step 5 tests and AC-3. No rig change: the prototype has no hosted lookup. Timestamp: the observed edit time.

Addressed the fifth review (Codex): uniqueness binds ID bytes to the proven key, with a table rebuild to drop the string-only constraint; the capability check runs only when a ceremony needs related origins; AC-4 requires adoption on beta first; step 6 states the hosted start/verify replacement. Rig rerun adds the spoofed-rawId scenario G and the adopt-first journey. Timestamp: the observed rig rerun.

Addressed the sixth review (Codex): step 6 no longer claims the local check covers the hosted verdict, since it never reads the signature counter and the hosted lookup returns none; new decision 9 asks whether the directory tracks the counter (recommended: no, because the deployed validator ignores it and synced passkeys report 0), with the tracking design and its tests in step 6 and AC-12. No rig change. Timestamp: the observed edit time.

Addressed the seventh review (Codex, five findings): every stored key has one spelling so the pair index can't be bypassed, and the hosted fallback compares keys by point; a failed directory lookup keeps today's hosted sign-in, verdict included; the completion takes no browser ID, and the lookup's signingId is credentialKey; step 9 rewrites the builder passkey page; step 3 raises user_version from 8 to 9 with tests. No rig change. Timestamp: the observed edit time.

Addressed the eighth review (Codex, three findings): the account row's draft copy promises other sites only in browsers that allow it and on devices that have the passkey; gg_startPasskeyAdoption takes the name and domain, its challenge is stored with them and the origin, and completion must match all three; step 5 extends the agent's Production Checklist and AC-13 requires a restore rehearsal before step 5 deploys. Also corrected which refusals the rig ran. No rig change. Timestamp: the observed edit time.

Addressed the ninth review (Codex, four findings): every insert writes credentialKey, registration included, and both stores' duplicate check moves to the ID-and-key pair; the shared check takes bytes and the completion's assertion travels as base64url JSON decoded at the route, tested through the real JSON-RPC route; the device walk adds a September www account on admin, the brief's success signal; a related-origins failure in a browser that reported support gets neutral copy. No rig change. Timestamp: the observed edit time.

Addressed CodeRabbit's review of cd46bf895: R6 now limits the neutral related-origins copy to a cross-site SecurityError in a browser that reported support or can't report it, as step 9 does, and step 9 adds a test that a NotAllowedError keeps its own copy. Timestamp: the observed edit time.

Addressed the tenth review (Codex, four findings): the account row compares the directory entry with the session's passkey, so a name held by another passkey keeps the row and its rename; a workflow test drives the saved-session hook through start, ceremony and completion; step 9 includes the two workflows that know the entry's domain and the hosted lookup, carrying that context to the copy; on www and beta a hosted name's refusal starts with Try again here. No rig change. Timestamp: the observed edit time.

Addressed the eleventh review (Codex, one finding): uniqueness now follows the account, the exact credentialId with the key, not the passkey, because the other ID spelling is another Kernel account and the app keeps a cached legacy spelling; that spelling may adopt under another name in either order, and the account row compares exact ID strings. Reverses the earlier rule the prototype held, so that case is a planned test. No rig change. Timestamp: the observed edit time.

Addressed the twelfth review (Codex, two findings): after adoption the saved-session hook saves the adopted name with setStoredUsername, with a remount test; the account-screen button reports busy, cancelled and failed states, with new failed copy in en, es and pt and tests. No rig change. Timestamp: the observed edit time.

Addressed the thirteenth review (Codex, one finding): step 1 makes switchingAccounts compare the exact ID string as well as the key, so a device that cached a legacy spelling signs in by both names, each to its own address, with a test and AC-1. No rig change. Timestamp: the observed edit time.

Addressed CodeRabbit's review of a0dcfbc46: completion writes the challenge's domain and origin to the adopted row's existing rpId and origin columns (spec contract and store, step 5 rule 11, the store test and AC-2). Timestamp: the observed edit time.

Logged Codex's finding on fa5cc950e as open item O1 in plan.todo.md (an omitted relatedOrigins key is unknown; attempt the ceremony), per Afo's direction to record later findings for implementation instead of fixing them in this PR. Timestamp: the observed edit time.

Logged Codex's five findings on bf45b41ac as open items O2 to O6 in plan.todo.md (structured refusal reasons, name validation at start and completion, app-made sign-ins and decision 2, telemetry proof, the challenge's wire form), per Afo's direction. Timestamp: the observed edit time.

Recorded Afo's answers: the plan's recommendations for decisions 1 to 7 and 9, with O4 settled under decision 2 (Use this device's passkey adopts inside its sign-in, its challenge requested when the sign-in screen offers the remembered passkey). Decision 9's tracking design is kept only as the option not taken. Timestamp: the observed edit time.
